paper.title_en: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
paper.abstract_en: While quantum state exclusion has received considerable attention, the analogous task of measurement outcome exclusion remains less explored. Here we develop a quantitative description of outcome exclusion and extend the resulting framework to obtain necessary and sufficient criteria for measurement simulation by quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing. Our analysis combines two approaches. Algebraic exclusion indices quantify normalized minimum errors in communication tasks with forbidden outputs and yield lower bounds on the number of classical messages required to reproduce the task statistics. Random exclusion profiles provide a statistical description in terms of optimized hypothesis-testing errors and are monotone under both types of processing. This connects outcome exclusion with statistical comparison in the spirit of Blackwell, linking the ability to suppress measurement outcomes to the possibility of simulating one measurement from another.
